title: Oblique Triangles Checkpoint
description: Show that you can classify triangles, identify given cases, and choose appropriate strategies.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 49°, 41°, and 90°. Which classification is correct?
questions.explanation: The triangle has a 90° angle, so it is a right triangle.

questions.question: A triangle has two known angles: 33° and 78°. What classification follows after finding the third angle?
questions.explanation: The third angle is 180° - 33° - 78° = 69°. All angles are less than 90°, so the triangle is acute oblique.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 22°, 47°, and 111°. Which classification is correct?
questions.explanation: No angle is 90°, so it is oblique. The 111° angle makes it obtuse.

questions.question: In △ABC, AB = 10 cm, BC = 14 cm, and AC = 18 cm are known. Which given case is shown?
questions.explanation: All three side lengths are known, so the given case is SSS.

questions.question: In △ABC, AB = 12 cm, AC = 7 cm, and ∠A = 52° are known. Which given case is shown?
questions.explanation: The angle ∠A is between sides AB and AC, so the case is SAS.

questions.question: In △XYZ, ∠X = 44°, ∠Y = 73°, and side XZ is known. Side XZ is not between the two given angles. Which case is shown?
questions.explanation: Two angles and a non-included side form the AAS case.

questions.question: Which given case can be ambiguous when solving oblique triangles?
questions.explanation: SSA may create zero, one, or two possible triangles, so it must be checked carefully.

questions.question: An oblique triangle has SAS information. Which strategy is usually the best starting point later?
questions.explanation: For SAS in an oblique triangle, the Law of Cosines is usually the best starting point.

questions.question: Explain in one or two sentences why an acute triangle is an oblique triangle.
questions.correctAnswer: An acute triangle has all angles less than 90°, so it has no right angle. Since an oblique triangle is any triangle with no 90° angle, an acute triangle is oblique.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that oblique means no right angle; all acute triangles meet that condition.

questions.question: A student says SAS and SSA are the same because both include two sides and one angle. Explain the difference.
questions.correctAnswer: In SAS, the known angle is included between the two known sides. In SSA, the known angle is not between the two known sides.
questions.explanation: The location of the angle matters because it changes the given case and the solving strategy.
